description:
ONE OF THE FOLDER'S TWO CLOSE FAILURES, and one of only two cases in it that combine a completely successful read pass with an abend - case18 states the same close-site arm over a single inline row, and this case states it over three fixture rows. app/cbl/CBACT02C.cbl:136-152 is 9000-CARDFILE-CLOSE, and :139 IF CARDFILE-STATUS = '00' is two-armed exactly as the open at :121 is, so anything other than '00' falls to :142 and the arm at :147-150 runs. What separates this case from the eight other abending cases in this directory is WHERE it abends: the open succeeded, all three seeded records were read and displayed, and the loop ended on a clean end-of-file, so nothing whatever was wrong with the data. THE END BANNER IS THEREFORE ABSENT, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE THESIS OF THIS CASE. The mainline runs :83 PERFORM 9000-CARDFILE-CLOSE, then :85 DISPLAY 'END OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBACT02C', then :87 GOBACK. Because :150's PERFORM 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM reaches CALL 'CEE3ABD' at :158 and never returns, :85 is never executed and the end banner is never emitted - even though every record was processed perfectly. A translation that wrote it anyway 'because the records all came through fine' would be wrong, and keeping the asymmetry is preserved behaviour under practice B5 rather than a defect to smooth over. THE SEVEN EXPECTED LINES, IN ORDER: :71's start banner (38 characters); the three 150-character record images from :78 DISPLAY CARD-RECORD, one per record, because :96's second DISPLAY is commented out and contributes nothing; :147's 'ERROR CLOSING CARDFILE' (22); :149's status line through 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS (24); and :155's 'ABENDING PROGRAM' (16). THE ARITHMETIC IDIOM, CHECKED FOR EQUIVALENCE: this paragraph spells the same 8/0/12 ladder the open paragraph writes with plain MOVEs. :137 ADD 8 TO ZERO GIVING APPL-RESULT deposits 8; :140 SUBTRACT APPL-RESULT FROM APPL-RESULT subtracts the field from itself and so always leaves 0; :142 ADD 12 TO ZERO GIVING APPL-RESULT deposits 12. The results are identical to the MOVE 8, MOVE 0 and MOVE 12 at :119, :122 and :124, the difference is purely stylistic, and no significance is read into it - the equivalence is recorded here so a reviewer can see it was checked rather than assumed. The 8 that :137 deposits never reaches the RETURN-CODE, because :139-143 always overwrites it before :144 IF APPL-AOK reads it, so expectedReturnCode is 12, carried with ABCODE 999 (:157) and TIMING 0 (:156). THE STATUS LINE, AND ONE DOCUMENTED DEVIATION. :148 moves CARDFILE-STATUS into IO-STATUS and :149 renders it. Under a COBOL runtime a close that cannot complete typically reports FILE STATUS '42' - CLOSE of a file that is not open - which is numeric with a first character other than '9' and would take the ELSE arm at :170-172, where MOVE '0000' TO IO-STATUS-04 followed by MOVE IO-STATUS TO IO-STATUS-04(3:2) gives the image '0042'. This translation cannot report that status and deliberately does not fabricate it: CardRepository.CardBrowse.endBrowse() returns void, so a failing close has no two-character status channel at all - it can only refuse - and AccountBalanceReaderJob reports the refusal under COBOL's own permanent-error convention, a status whose first byte is '9' carrying a binary feedback code in its second. That is precisely the condition :162-163 tests for, IF IO-STATUS NOT NUMERIC OR IO-STAT1 = '9', so :164-168 run instead: IO-STAT1 moves to position one, a two-byte binary is zeroed, its low-order byte is overwritten with IO-STAT2, and the result moves into a PIC 999 receiver - giving the image '9000', because a translated data-access refusal carries no VSAM feedback code to report and inventing one would put a number in the log that no backend produced. This case therefore pins that arm at the CLOSE site, which nothing else in this directory reaches: case09 and case10 pin it at the OPEN site and case13 at the READ site, and each of those three records the same refusal to fabricate a two-digit code. The trailing NNNN of 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' really is part of the COBOL literal at :168 and :172 and is not a placeholder awaiting substitution; it is reproduced verbatim and must never be 'corrected'. WHY THE INDUCEMENT IS A STUB AND NOT DATA. A close failure cannot be produced from input data under any circumstances: by the time :138 runs, every record has already been read successfully, so no row, no width and no key can reach this arm. This is the case in the folder most dependent on a forced outcome, and it is said plainly here rather than left implicit (practice B12). ParityCase carries no member for it - a BATCH_JOB case is refused a screenRequest, and the forced-outcome vocabulary covers read, readForUpdate, readNext, startBrowse, write, rewrite and delete but no close - so nothing is invented in this file. The inducement belongs to CBACT02CParityTest, whose Scenario.closeFailing() delivers every seeded row, ends the loop on a clean end-of-file and then refuses endBrowse(). The call sequence this case exercises (gate G47) is openBrowse reporting '00', readNext normal three times, readNext reporting '10', then endBrowse refused. openBrowse and not startBrowse, deliberately: :121 tests the open's own status, and reading through the online startBrowse - which reports none - would leave :129-132 unreachable. THE INPUT. CARDFILE is seeded with rows 1 to 3 of app/data/ASCII/carddata.txt through the fixture form, fromRow 0 and rowCount 3, which is the same seeding case06 declares - so the three expected images are byte-identical to the fixture by construction rather than by transcription. Three records rather than fifty keeps the file readable while still proving the read pass ran to completion, and sharing case06's input makes the pair directly comparable: identical data and identical first four lines, then a clean CLOSE and the end banner there against a refused CLOSE and a lost banner here. The rows are 0500024453765740 (Aniya Von, 2023-03-09), 0683586198171516 (Ward Jones, 2025-07-13) and 0923877193247330 (Enrico Rosenbaum, 2024-08-11), in ascending CARD-NUM order, which is the order :31's ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL over :32's RECORD KEY IS FD-CARD-NUM delivers them in. Each image is exactly 150 characters and ends in the 59 spaces of app/cpy/CVACT02Y.cpy's trailing FILLER X(59): CARD-NUM X(16) at 1-16, CARD-ACCT-ID 9(11) at 17-27, CARD-CVV-CD 9(03) at 28-30, CARD-EMBOSSED-NAME X(50) at 31-80, CARD-EXPIRAION-DATE X(10) - misspelled in the copybook and left misspelled here - at 81-90, CARD-ACTIVE-STATUS X(01) at 91, and FILLER X(59) at 92-150 (gates G19 and G21). expectedWrites and expectedFinalState are empty as positive assertions rather than as omissions: :120 opens the file INPUT and the program contains no WRITE, REWRITE or DELETE, so nothing is written on any path, abending or not. The code page is US-ASCII, named explicitly and never taken from the platform. NAMING (rule R1, register 0.8.4): the unit is account.AccountBalanceReaderJob, an 'Account'-named class in the account package, but CBACT02C reads the CARD file - app/jcl/READCARD.jcl:25-26 binds DD CARDFILE and the program's only SELECT at :29 assigns to it, and no balance is read, computed or written anywhere. The name is the prompt's and is honoured verbatim; the behaviour is the source's. The dataset is addressed only through its CARDFILE binding key and never by a dataset name (gate G46), and the unit is reached at tasklet level with no JobLauncher and no HTTP in the path (gate G51). PROVENANCE: every expected value here is statically derived - by structured reading of app/cbl/CBACT02C.cbl cross-checked against app/cpy/CVACT02Y.cpy, app/jcl/READCARD.jcl and the real app/data/ASCII/carddata.txt - and none of it was captured from a live COBOL run, because executing these programs is empirically impossible in this environment (Agent Action Plan 0.7.6, eight independently verified blockers, risk R-A).

HOW THE OUTCOME IS ARRANGED, DECLARED RATHER THAN SELECTED IN JAVA. This case arranges a CLOSE refused after the whole input has been read and displayed: unitStimulus.callSiteOutcomes names CLOSE-CARDFILE and gives it a refusal. It is declared here because a case identifier must name a case and never configure one - the shape used to be chosen by a switch over 'case01'..'case20' in CBACT02CParityTest, so this file showed the abend lines and said nothing about the condition that produced them, and renumbering a case silently changed what it ran. A case that names no call site reads its whole input and closes cleanly, so silence here is itself a statement. The outcome is a CICS RESP rather than a FILE STATUS because CardRepository reports this program's card-file outcomes as responses and AccountBalanceReaderJob translates them - declaring a status directly would skip the translation the case exists to judge.
